abstract: Recent advancements in protein structure prediction methods have ushered in a new era of abundant and accurate structural data, providing opportunities to analyse proteins at a scale that has not been possible before. Here we performed a large-scale analysis of physicochemical properties across 373,779 confident AlphaFold structures. Our analysis revealed systematic variation between proteins from different organisms to such an extent that major features of the tree of life could be recovered from these data. Surprisingly, this relationship persisted even when we restricted our analysis to eukaryotic, cytosolic proteins and proteins from single AlphaFold Database Foldseek clusters. Given the strong functional constraints on protein chemistry, this finding is unexpected and suggests that protein structures have organism-specific physicochemical signatures, which might reveal evolutionary constraints imposed by the cellular environment and could have significant implications for the design and engineering of novel proteins.
